title: Batch versus online inference
prompt: A shop wants to score every item overnight and answer a personalised prediction request while a customer waits. Which inference mode fits each job, and what constraints drive your choice?
objective: Choose batch or online inference based on how soon predictions must be available.
expected_scope: Match each job to a mode and compare response-time, scheduling or throughput considerations.
hint: Ask whether the person using the prediction can wait for a scheduled job.
reference_explanation: Use batch inference for the overnight catalogue run. It can process a large group of items in a scheduled job and save the results for later. Use online inference for a customer who needs a prediction computed from the current request, because the service needs to respond with low latency. Batch may amortise setup across many records. Online serving needs capacity when requests arrive.

criteria.description: Chooses batch inference for the scheduled catalogue job and explains why.
Chooses online inference for an on-demand request and explains the latency constraint.
Explains a throughput, scheduling or serving capacity trade-off.

critical_misconceptions: Saying that ‘online inference’ means the model retrains with every request.
